title: Two-argument oracle-call step
statement: Let $\ell$ be a label, $j\in\{0,1,2,3,4\}$, and $r,r'\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, and let $v$ assign a natural number to each of the four registers. If the instruction at $\ell$ calls oracle $j$ in unary-first mode with the ordered registers $r,r'$, with successor labels $\ell_1$ and $\ell_0$ for positive and negative answers, respectively, then one machine step from the configuration with label $\ell$, registers $v$, and no answer leaves the registers unchanged and no answer recorded, and moves to $\ell_1$ exactly when the oracle accepts the encoding of $1^n$ paired with the encoding of the binary representations of $v(r)$ and $v(r')$; otherwise it moves to $\ell_0$.
hypotheses_covered: The instruction at $\ell$ is the specified ordered two-register oracle call
The registers $r,r'$ lie among the four registers
